newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIANS WIN U.S. COLLEGIATE CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIANS WIN U.S. COLLEGIATE CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Australian Luke Smith won the singles and teamed with countryman Tim Blenkiron to take the doubles for the University of Nevada at Las Vegas at the U.S. national collegiate tennis championships Sunday.

Smith, a UNLV senior from Adelaide, used a strong serve and volley game to beat George Bastl from Villars, Switzerland, representing the University of Southern California, 6-4 6-3 in the singles final at the University of California at Los Angeles.
Smith and Blenkiron, from Woodside, Australia, then beat Bastl and Californian Kyle Spencer 6-4 6-4.
It was the first time since 1966 that the singles and doubles competitors had squared off in both championship finals.

Smith, unseeded in both events, became just the second player in the last 20 years of National Collegiate Athletics Association championship action to capture both singles and doubles titles in the same year. In 1992, Alex O'Brien of Stanford University won both NCAA championships.
Smith, the first unseeded singles champion since Stanford's Jared Palmer won it in 1991, did not lose a set in the nine-day tournament despite his 65th ranking coming in.
Smith and Blenkiron became the first unseeded duo to win the doubles championship since 1989 when Eric Amend and Byron Black did it for USC.
